correlates.name: Hypertension with Diabetes, CKD and Left Ventricular Hypertrophy
correlates.pathophysiology: diabetes, chronic kidney disease and hypertension share a metabolic background and insulin resistance, so they cluster in the same patient . Sustained pressure load produces LVH; diabetic nephropathy raises creatinine.
correlates.treatment: add an ACE inhibitor. It improves remodeling of LVH and slows progression of chronic kidney disease in diabetic nephropathy - the one agent that treats all three problems at once.

correlates.name: ACE Inhibitor-Associated Angioedema
correlates.pathophysiology: ACE inhibition prevents degradation of vasoactive peptides, producing non-pitting swelling of the lips, tongue and airway.
correlates.treatment: stop the ACE inhibitor and transition to an ARB.

correlates.name: Hypertensive Urgency
correlates.presentation: SBP 180 or more or DBP 120 or more, without signs or symptoms of acute end-organ damage. Confirm the absence: no headache, no chest pain, unremarkable labs, and a normal fundus with no hemorrhages or papilledema.
correlates.treatment: still treat - short-acting oral agent first, then transition to long-acting.

correlates.name: Hypertensive Emergency
correlates.presentation: severe headache, blurred vision, chest pain, flash pulmonary edema with wheezing and crackles, LVH or ischemic changes on ECG, or acute kidney injury with a rising creatinine.
correlates.treatment: admit to the ICU. Start a short-acting IV antihypertensive, e.g. the vasodilator hydralazine, and monitor. First hour: drop MAP no more than 20%. Next 23 hours: 5-10% further, to about 160/110. Then normalize over 24-48 hours.

correlates.name: NSAID-Induced Blood Pressure Elevation
correlates.presentation: an apparently non-responsive hypertensive whose medication list includes a chronic NSAID - here, ibuprofen taken for osteoarthritis.
correlates.pathophysiology: NSAIDs raise blood pressure and antagonize the mechanism by which antihypertensives work, blunting the response to therapy .
correlates.treatment: counsel on NSAID use and substitute an analgesic that does not raise blood pressure, e.g. acetaminophen (Tylenol Extra Strength) or another headache agent.

correlates.name: Resistant Hypertension
correlates.presentation: blood pressure uncontrolled on three medications, one of which is a diuretic, each at the maximally tolerated dose - or controlled only on four medications.
correlates.treatment: consult a hypertension specialist. Adjunctive options include an aldosterone antagonist, beta blocker, direct vasodilator or alpha-2 agonist; clonidine is added to first-line therapy in this setting rather than used as monotherapy.
